newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Political worries shadow Bangladesh anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Political worries shadow Bangladesh anniversary.

text.p: Bangladesh went ahead on Saturday with preparations for a star-studded independence anniversary celebration next week despite a looming nationwide general strike which poses a major challenge to the government.
The government kicked off a dress rehearsal for Wednesday's independence celebrations with a rally by leading entertainers and other celebrities.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who took office last June, faces a major test on Sunday in the eight-hour national strike called by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
Khaleda has urged Bangladeshis to join in the strike as a way of helping to topple what she called the "repressive, pro-Indian rule" of Hasina's political party, the Awami League.

Hasina left for Pakistan on Saturday to attend a one-day summit of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC). The country's 26th independence anniversary is expected to be attended by South African President Nelson Mandela, Turkish President Suleyman Demirel and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, officials said on Saturday.

"We are expecting a star-studded anniversary," one official told Reuters. "But the BNP-led strike is causing some worry," he said. The country's business community was also worried over the strike, seeing it as a potential threat to exports and efforts to lure foreign investment.
Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said its leaders had met Khaleda on Friday and requested her to call off the strike.
"She (Khaleda) is acting too hastily," said one bank official, who declined to be identified.
Police said they had been asked by authorities not to handle strikers too harshly.
Hasina on Friday asked Awami League leaders and workers to stay calm and go ahead with preparations for the celebrations.
Wednesday's anniversary programmes would include a massive children's show, and return of the "independence torch" to capital Dhaka after a cross-country rally.
The rally began on March 7 when Hasina handed the torch to two veterans of the 1971 independence war. She will receive it back on Wednesday.
The visiting dignitaries are expected to be with Hasina at both ceremonies, officials said.
Hasina's father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, who led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan in 1971, was killed in a 1975 army coup that ended a short spell of rule by his Awami League.

His daughter regained power in a general election last June but has yet to fully restore political stability, which Bangladesh's overseas donors, including the World Bank, say is essential for attracting investors.
As Hasina boarded the plane to Islamabad, hundreds of Urdu-speaking Bihari Moslems, stranded in Bangladesh since 1971 hoping to migrate to Pakistan, joined an open-air prayer session in Dhaka.

"We are praying so that Hasina can persuade (Pakistan) Prime Minister Newaz Sharif to repatriate us soon. We have lived like animals in refugee camps over past 25 years," said Bihari leader Mohammad Nasim Khan.
